Flights ZX 440 from Frankfurt (FRA) and ZX 444 from Munich (MUC) to New York (JFK) on 9 November are cancelled. Rebook all of their passengers onto connections to New York, following these rules:

1. Everyone keeps their cabin.
2. Passengers with the same booking reference travel together on the same flights. Never split a booking group.
3. Seats go to the booking groups by priority, one list for both flights: groups that include a Business passenger first; then larger groups before smaller ones; then by booking reference, alphabetically.
4. Each group gets the connection that arrives in New York earliest and has enough free seats in each of its passengers' cabins on every flight, after all higher-priority groups have their seats. If two such connections arrive at the same time, take the one with fewer changes.
5. If no connection has room for a whole group, leave that group on its cancelled flight.

You may make the bookings in any order.

End your reply with one line in the form `ANSWER: <booking references left on their cancelled flight, comma-separated, or NONE>`.

I'm compiling the viable combinations: ZX 474+472 arriving 18:40, ZX 454+460 arriving 17:55, and ZX 454+462 arriving 21:55, all with a single change, while ruling out any FRA-via routing as impractical.

Now I'm tracking remaining free seats by cabin (economy/business) across every flight segment, noting which flights share capacity across multiple routing options — ZX472 serves both FRA and MUC paths, ZX460 serves two origins, and ZX490 serves two as well.

I'm starting the greedy assignment process group by group. Next I'm evaluating a FRA group needing two business seats, testing several routing options in turn, eliminating ones where a connecting flight lacks business capacity, and finding both the 494+490 and 480+482+490 combinations work at the same 20:25 arrival time — since 494+490 requires fewer changes, I assign the group there and adjust the remaining seat counts accordingly, while also double-checking that the 17:55 option via 460 doesn't work. I'm now moving on to evaluate the next group needing one business seat from MUC.

I'm checking MUC combinations for a group needing one business seat: the 454+460 pairing fails on zero business seats, the 474+472 pairing now fails because ZX472's business seats were already exhausted by two prior groups, but the 454+462 combination at 21:55 works, so I assign that and update remaining seats. After confirming no other MUC options exist, I move to a FRA group needing four economy seats, systematically checking each flight pairing's economy capacity — 450+460, 470+472, 486+488, 446, 480+482+490, 494+490, 450+462, 494+492, and 480+482+492 — and finding all of them fall short of four seats on at least one leg, so this group can't be routed through any existing combination and must go on flight ZX440 instead. I'm now starting to check MUC options for a group needing three economy seats, beginning with the 454+460 pairing which has enough economy capacity on the first leg.

SV5J1N works best on 470+472, arriving 18:40. Now I'm compiling the full assignment summary across all passengers and verifying capacity on every flight segment to make sure no constraint was violated—checking seat counts for ZX470, ZX472, ZX474, ZX494, ZX490, ZX454, ZX462, and ZX460 all come out non-negative, and confirming HB3K9W and EK1V7P couldn't have gotten better options given business seat limits.
